Open Start and type your company name and your own rules in the yellow cells: deposit share, the price from which a deposit is asked, quote validity, rush rule, cancellation window and sales tax.
Type every new order on Orders. The lead time, total, balance after the deposit, deposit flag and rush flag fill in. Copy the first rows to see how a full order looks.
Record every deposit on Deposits: the due date, the paid date and the method. The days late and the status show who still owes a deposit, and Payments keeps the full list of money received.
Send each quote from Quotes and fill the status. Quotes with no reply after the warning days are flagged, and Quote follow-ups keeps the outcome of each call or message.
Write every enquiry on Enquiries with the channel, the occasion, the wanted date and the budget. Enquiries waiting more than a few days show first.
Before you say yes to a date, read Daily order limits: cakes and tiered cakes booked against the limit. Put clients for a full day on the Waiting list.
Write the theme, the colours and the message on Design briefs, and fill the approval date when the client agrees. Unapproved briefs stay marked.
Note every allergy on Allergy notes with who checked it. The recipe check compares the allergy with the allergens of the product.
Use Order changes and Cancellations to keep the old and the new total, the deposit kept and the refund. The Cancellation refund calculator applies your rule.
Check Occasion calendar every month for order cut-off dates, and Reminders for birthdays and anniversaries of repeat clients.

Use the 14 calculators before you answer: order total, deposit, lead time, cake capacity, quote dates, order change, cancellation refund, enquiry conversion, guests, boxes, rush surcharge, profit, balance reminder and a what-if grid.
Read the Orders and Deposits Dashboard and Charts every week: orders by month, channel, occasion and decoration, quote status, enquiries, deposits and cancellations.

The orders to bake and hand over by due date; the days to the due date, the day to start the work, the lead time and the rush check fill in by themselves.
Production tasks by day and person
One row for each bake, fill and cover, decorate or pack task with the day, the person and the hours; the flag shows what is overdue, due today or done late.
Hours for each person and day against their day
One row for each person and day with the tasks, the hours and the hours the person can work; the load percent, the free hours and the overload flag fill in.
Daily plan with oven and fridge load
One row for each day with the orders and units due, the hours for each kind of work, the oven tray loads, the fridge slots and the team hours; the oven load, the fridge load and the flags fill in.
Products with labour minutes, tray loads and shelf days
The 24 products with the labour minutes, the oven tray loads, the fridge slots and the shelf days that the plan uses; the hours for one unit and the units in a tray load fill in.
Standing orders baked for cafes and shops
The same products delivered every week to cafes and shops; the delivery days, the units for each delivery, the tray loads and the days to the renewal fill in.
Shifts with overtime hours and cost
One row for each shift with the start and the hours worked; the overtime hours over a normal shift, their cost and the overtime flag fill in.
Bake batches with oven minutes and tray loads
One row for each bake of a recipe (a batch) with the batches, the tray loads, the baker and the oven minutes; the tray loads for each oven hour fill in.
One row for each time block of the oven day with the program, the product group and the tray loads booked; the free trays, the block load and the flag fill in.
The ovens, mixers, fridges, proofer and decorating tools with their capacity and service dates; the days to the next service and the service flag fill in.
The decorated cakes waiting for a decorator with the hours and the due date; the days left, the hours needed each day and a tight flag fill in, so a cake with too little time shows first.
One row for each night with the finished items held and the slots used against the fridge capacity; the free slots, the fridge load and the full flag fill in.
Ingredient needs by day against stock on hand
The main ingredients the bakes of each day need against the stock on hand; the shortage and a shortage flag fill in, so a missing ingredient shows before the bake.
Holiday peaks with expected orders and extra hours
The busy periods of the year with the expected orders and the extra staff hours; the days to the start, the length, the orders a day and the state fill in.
Delays with minutes lost and their cost
One row for each task that ran late with the minutes late, the reason and the people waiting; the cost of the delay and the kind of task fill in.
Rework with hours lost and its cost
One row each time a cake or box was made again with what went wrong and the hours lost; the cost, the client and the product fill in.
Time off with days and answer
One row for each time off request with the dates, the kind and the answer; the days, the state and a flag for a request with no answer fill in.
The limits the plan is checked against: tray loads, fridge slots, decorating hours, tiered cakes and rush orders for one day.
Prep list by day and person
The preparation done before a bake or decorating day, such as layers, buttercream, syrup, fillings and labels; the status and the person phone fill in, so a late prep job shows first.
